name: Idaho
nameStory: Idaho is the one state name that was simply made up. A lobbyist named George Willing told Congress it was Shoshone for 'gem of the mountains.' It wasn't - he invented it. The hoax was exposed, Congress gave the name Colorado to that territory instead, and then Idaho got stuck on a different territory anyway.
capitalStory: French trappers crossing the treeless Snake River plain finally spotted a line of cottonwoods along a river and shouted 'les bois!' - 'the woods!' The capital of Idaho is named after the relief of seeing trees.

majorFeatures.name: Snake River
majorFeatures.note: Curves across the whole southern state

majorFeatures.name: Hells Canyon
majorFeatures.note: Deepest river gorge in North America

majorFeatures.name: Sawtooth Mountains
majorFeatures.note: Jagged granite peaks in the center

funFacts: Hells Canyon is deeper than the Grand Canyon.
About a third of all potatoes grown in the United States come from Idaho.
Idaho has more designated wilderness than any state except Alaska.
The Salmon River was called the River of No Return because boats could ride it downstream but never fight back up.
